floor_history.headline: Recon: pins removed, honest floor 20 -> 14; structure fully explained (loop1 = for/array-index via loop.c givs, loop2 = goto-form pointer walk); remaining 14 = two register 2-cycles with measured allo

frontier.hypothesis: Loop-2 k<->a3off swap closes by shaving k's priority margin (.278 vs .276): one fewer counted ref or ~2 more live insns on k flips the alloc order
frontier.mechanism: global.c allocno_compare; k needs to allocate AFTER a3off, then k's conflict set (a0temp/pa1/pa2/a3off) forces it into t0 = target
frontier.next_probe: spelling sweep on k's tail ops (k++ placement, k+=1, test k<9 vs k!=9, s16 k) measuring lreg refs/live each time; verify with greg.sh dispositions before sandboxing

frontier.hypothesis: Loop-1 i->t0/judge->a2 needs the merged counter (conflict with loop-2 a2/a3 holders) with total counted refs <=7 so prio .222 sits below pa2 .286 and a3off .276
frontier.mechanism: floor_log2(7)=2 vs floor_log2(8+)=3; judge-base (.12) then allocates after i and shares a2 with pa2 (disjoint live ranges) = target
frontier.next_probe: rebuild merged form, dump lreg FIRST (session 1 never measured merged refs - guessing wasted a probe), then tune ++/test spellings to hit <=7 refs

frontier.hypothesis: If manual priority tuning stalls, the remaining space is small enough for a directed permuter campaign from the 14-floor base
frontier.mechanism: pure-rename residual; permuter sweeps statement order/spellings mechanically
frontier.next_probe: clean single-function target.o (offset 0), seed = candidate.c, PERM sweep on init order + counter spellings, fresh-seed discipline
